methodological_rigor.justification: Multicentric (three tertiary hospitals in Cote d'Ivoire) retrospective cohort of 195 patients with breast cancer receiving NAC from 2017-2024, with prespecified inclusion/exclusion criteria and AJCC 8th-edition staging. Pathology and IHC were performed locally at different labs (acknowledged limitation), Ki67 was not available, and a large fraction of HER2-positive patients did not receive anti-HER2 therapy as part of NAC due to testing delays, all of which confound interpretation. Appropriate analytic strategy: binary logistic regression for pCR predictors, Kaplan-Meier with log-rank univariate, Cox multivariate with variable selection based on univariate P<0.05. HER2 trial-independent variables and molecular heterogeneity not fully controlled; no adjustment for confounders across sites; no power calculation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort (Oxford 2b) addressing pCR after NAC and survival in an under-represented Black West African population. Clinical relevance is high because most supporting data for pCR as a surrogate endpoint come from European/North American cohorts, and this study provides direct West African evidence (e.g., 40% TN rate, confirmed pCR as strongest independent predictor of PFS/OS). Findings may inform regional treatment strategies and advocacy for better access to HER2-directed and platinum agents.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the relevant standard. The paper reports setting, eligibility, variable definitions (pCR, PFS, OS), statistical methods, and effect estimates with 95% CIs for ORs and HRs. Gaps relative to STROBE include no explicit flow diagram, incomplete handling of loss-to-follow-up patients (addressed by exclusion rather than characterization), no sensitivity analyses, limited discussion of bias beyond retrospective design and lack of Ki67, and no centralized pathology. No data-sharing statement or deposit of de-identified dataset.

novelty_literature.justification: The biological question (pCR as surrogate predictor of survival in breast cancer NAC) is well established in multiple large meta-analyses (Cortazar 2014, Spring 2020, cited by authors) and is not novel per se. The novelty lies in the population: first such analysis of pCR-survival relationships in Cote d'Ivoire patients, confirming that pCR remains the strongest independent PFS/OS predictor in a Black West African cohort with high (40%) TN prevalence. This is a meaningful population-specific extension rather than a conceptual advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally well organized with typical clinical-paper structure. Results tables and Kaplan-Meier figures are referenced. Some grammatical and typographic issues appear (e.g., missing closing parentheses, 'Odd ratio' spelling, 'intensify NAC' usage), and a few sentences lose clarity (e.g., HER2 scoring description is truncated mid-sentence). Overall readability is adequate; the discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within AR-negative/QNBC literature and sub-Saharan African treatment access.

key_strengths: Multi-center (3 tertiary centers) West African cohort addresses an under-represented population in NAC/pCR evidence base
pCR confirmed as the strongest independent predictor of PFS (HR 6.54) and OS (HR 5.84) in this cohort
Subtype-specific analysis demonstrates pCR is associated with significantly improved OS in TN subtype, consistent with global findings
Appropriate statistical analyses (logistic regression for pCR predictors; KM/log-rank/Cox for survival)
key_concerns: Retrospective design with decentralized pathology and IHC, no central review, no Ki67 data

Confounding: only 32.5% of HER2-positive patients received anti-HER2 as part of NAC and only 3.8% of TN patients received carboplatin, limiting relevance to contemporary standard-of-care pCR benchmarks
No explicit handling or description of missing data or loss-to-follow-up characteristics
STROBE reporting incomplete (no flow diagram, limited bias and sensitivity analysis)
Novelty is population-specific rather than conceptual
chief_reviewer.rationale: A clinically relevant retrospective West African multicenter cohort that confirms pCR-survival associations but with decentralized pathology, incomplete contemporary systemic therapy exposure, and reporting gaps; best fit is a mid-tier specialty oncology journal after major revisions addressing STROBE adherence and confounding.
